newsitem.title: USA: Chubb considering sale of units - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Chubb considering sale of units - analysts.

text.p: Chubb Corp told Wall Street analysts in a conference call after the stock market close on Thursday that it is considering the possible sale of its life and real estate businesses, analysts said.
Chubb Corp was not immediately available for comment.
Chubb shares rose 4-1/8, or about nine percent, to 49-5/8 in active mid-morning trading.
Chubb shares closed down 3-1/2 at 45-1/2 on Thursday after the company reported disappointing third quarter earnings. Third quarter earnings were hurt by catastrophe losses and slow premium growth.
In the conference call, Chubb chief executive Dean O'Hare told analysts the company was considering the possible sale of the life and real estate units in a move to improve shareholder value.
Decisions about how to proceed could come as early as December, Smith Barney analyst Ron Frank said in a research note to the sales force.

Bear Stearns analyst Steven Gavios said Chubb may use the assets from the sale of those businesses to buy back shares, make acquisitions or build up the infrastructure of some of its other businesses.

The life operations currently have equity based on Generallly Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) of $842 million and the real estate operations have GAAP equity of $426 million, Gavios said in a morning research report.
Gavios upgraded the stock to buy from attractive and has a 12- to 18-month price target of at least $65 a share.
"We believe the sum of the parts is worth $65 a share or higher," Gavios said in a telephone interview with Reuters.

"We believe that Mr. O'Hare's patience has run out, with the turnaround at the life operations happening slower than expected, which pushed out the waiting time until the earnings performance would be up to par," Gavios said in his report.

"Additionally, with the dramatic consolidation of the life insurance industry going on today, Chubb has come to the realization that being a player in the life business would have required it to double down on its investment, which management did not think was prudent," Gavios said.

"Mr. O'Hare tells us that the company is well into the process of evaluating its alternatives and that it should make meaningful headway on the decision process by year-end," Gavios said in the report.
